body:
WorkerBackend workers are now tracked in a registry. Each add_workers call creates a launch group with a desired worker count. Each worker has one row holding its scheduler job id, Distributed id, output file, and state. The states are `starting` (submitted, queued, or connected and loading code), `ready` (in the pool), `busy` (running a member), and `ended`.

During a calibration the dispatch loop reconciles the registry with the scheduler and ends workers that are not ready within `startup_timeout` seconds of submission (12 hours by default), and launches replacements for any group below its desired count, up to that group's `max_relaunches`. The only other way to grow the pool mid-run is to call `add_workers` again. A worker that dies while running a member still counts as a failed member and its replacement picks up later members. A worker that fails to load its code is stopped, and its group launches no more workers, since a replacement would fail the same way. When the driver exits, an `atexit` hook cancels every job the session submitted.

Key changes
- New API: `worker_rows`, `worker_registry` and `set_registry_path!`
- Worker registry (`worker_registry.jl`): Each worker has one `WorkerRecord`, keyed by registry row ID.
- Each `add_workers` call now creates a `LaunchGroup` with desired number of workers and max relaunches (default 2*nworkers)
- Registry is written to a TOML file by default, this is not really necessary since existing Distributed workers cannot easily join a new main session but could be useful for debugging.
- Reconciliation (`worker_reconcile.jl`): reconciles the registry with the scheduler state via `qstat` or `squeue`.
    - Ends workers whose process has disconnected or that weren't found within the startup timeout
    - Queue replacement workers for launch groups below their desired count, up to the maximum
    -  A worker that fails to load its code stops its group from relaunching, since a replacement would fail the same way
- Added `Backend.Workers` module. Exported names are unchanged
- All submitted jobs are cancelled on exit via `cancel_worker_jobs`
- Queued jobs are awaited outside `addprocs`. Distributed's worker lock is held while `addprocs` is running, so we need to wait for workers outside of it.
title: Add worker registry with relaunch for WorkerBackend

body: closes https://github.com/CliMA/ClimaCalibrate.jl/issues/368, closes https://github.com/CliMA/ClimaCalibrate.jl/issues/368. This PR adds `AbstractTransform` which are lazy transformations applied to a `SampleCollection`. This is used by the `observation` method to get the original samples and pass the sample collection and transformations to the `covariance` methods. This implementation also does not require supplying the same keyword arguments for all the `covariance` methods and should make it simpler for users to create custom observation recipes.
title: Add transforms for sample collection
